user_hypothesis: Baskov and Bilan appear to be operated by the same SMM company on Threads.

evidence.finding: March 2026 reporting described Baskov, Bilan and Leps as part of the same sudden Threads activity wave, with users explicitly suspecting PR/SMM managers because of the volume and style of replies.

T-J observed Baskov, Bilan and Leps posting memes, replying to users, interacting with one another, and Baskov/Bilan sustaining a recurring 'main celebrity in Threads' rivalry; the author explicitly characterized celebrity shitposting as likely done by SMM managers.
A PR-consulting analysis described Baskov's stranger-reply strategy as a working celebrity communications tactic and noted that Bilan, Kirkorov and Leps were participating in the same mode.
A 2026 marketing article stated that Baskov 'brought' Bilan, Lazarev and Kirkorov into the Threads commenting trend, supporting campaign-style propagation but not common operator attribution.

negative_controls: Baskov and Bilan historically have distinct publicly reported management/PR structures; no current public source ties both to one named SMM agency.
Celebrity cross-talk can be organic, coordinated between separate teams, or platform-native imitation; shared style alone cannot distinguish these cases.
Public reporting that 'SMM managers probably write' is not proof of one common contractor.

requires_any_strong_bridge: same named SMM/PR agency or contractor
same employee publicly claiming both accounts
identical rare copy with prepublication timing inconsistent with imitation
leaked contract/invoice/portfolio or credible insider confirmation

best_current_assessment: Baskov and Bilan are clearly participating in the same Threads celebrity-engagement/reply-bait ecosystem and appear to use closely aligned communication tactics. Public evidence does not currently establish that one SMM company or one operator manages both accounts. The common-operator hypothesis is therefore a high-value platform-side question for Meta, not a public attribution claim.
